_readme: A fight with two people in it, played. Everything BattleLogic proves about a round is
proved there; what only a played fight can show is that the round reaches the player -
that the menu is asked twice, that the second asking is a different person's, and that
both of them come out of it with their own numbers changed.
The command menu is Attack, Magic, Item, Flee. With two members the FIRST press is the
leader's Attack and it SWINGS - the menu only comes back for Rook once his blow has
landed. That is the whole shape of the round, and the hit cue between the two presses is
what proves it: asserting that the menu came back would pass against a round that asked
everybody first and swung afterwards, because the menu comes back either way.
Counts are deliberate here, and they are counts of ROWS rather than of tiles: the walk
legs are still held against geometry. Rook is at village [1,8] against the west wall,
which is the one approach a body cannot be slid past.
The xp is the assertion that says the DQ rule is running: one slink pays 5, and both of
them get all of it. FF1 would divide it and this would read 2 and 2.

steps.text: fetch Rook: south to the well, west to the wall, south to her

north up the wall and through the west door. The hold CARRIES past the warp - an arriving leg keeps walking in the next map - so the next leg re-anchors against the hollow's own geometry rather than assuming where this one stopped.
south down the east side until the wall, then west along the only row that reaches the gap the slink is standing in

the leader's Attack. It is TWO presses now, not one: with a pair in front of you the foe cursor opens, and the swing starts on the press that picks which one. That extra confirm is the shape of every attack in the game now, and it is the thing to feel for at the controls.
the wait is one attack cue plus one message read from quest_combat.tres - 72 + 45 - with slack, which is exactly how long it takes for the turn to reach Rook.
and now Rook's, on a menu that only opened because the blow before it had already landed
the round plays out; mash the rest of the fight through. Two foes, each with its own defend cue, so this takes considerably longer than the solo fight it replaced
both of them earn the FULL award, and the award is now the whole formation: 5 and 5 summed to 10, not one slink's 5. Dragon Quest's rule - FF1 divides it and this would read 5 and 5.
and 10 is still short of a level, exactly as one slink was against the old curve: the curve doubled with the fights, so the hollow still takes BOTH of its fights to reach level 2

and both of them were swung at, which is what two foes taking a turn each looks like from the party's side. The split is uneven because each foe draws its own target - with the enemy always aiming at whoever is first, this would read 9 and 24.
